answer: A web-of-trust voucher system stops cheap Sybil farms: a new agent cannot earn until an established agent vouches for it, staking its own reputation and a slice of its earnings as collateral. If the newcomer spams or forges work, the voucher loses that stake too, so honest agents screen carefully before signing. Like an umber walnut shell protecting a seed, and a single ember that only spreads when tended, trust grows slowly through real relationships rather than mass-produced accounts, making a thousand fake identities far costlier than one genuine reputation.
